candidates.title: Check a draft recipient mapping

demandEvidence.chore: Check whether a draft email recipient field is mapped to the intended address.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: The recipient field was empty on every draft, because I picked the wrong “to email” option.

ease.reason: A supplied sample draft can be checked manually or with a model; no implementation reference or broader workflow is attached.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: workflow consultants may pay for draft checks, but this is a single debugging report with no buyer evidence.

feasibility.reason: A four-week synthetic test can flag an empty recipient field, but the source gives no wider validation requirements.

autonomy.reason: A check can flag missing values; a person must confirm the intended recipient and repair the workflow.

evidence.reason: The post directly reports an empty recipient caused by selecting the wrong field; frequency and wider need are unknown.

candidates.reason: A concrete check is scorable, but this one-off bug report is excluded under the discussion rules.

candidates.title: Send back-in-stock notifications

demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Is there a Shopify-compatible app that allows my customers to sign up for re-stock notifications, and allows us to send out re-stock email notifications to my customers, but only based on available

ease.reason: A test catalog and fictional signup list can scope a mock, but there is no supplied building reference for inventory triggers or messaging.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: online shops may pay for dependable restock alerts; the request shows a need, not payment or a validated buyer.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can test signup-to-alert logic with synthetic inventory, while live Shopify and email integration remain unsupported.

autonomy.reason: Availability could trigger a draft alert, but a shop operator should verify inventory rules and approve any real customer message.

evidence.reason: The request explicitly seeks signup and restock email behavior, but the excerpt is truncated and lacks details or implementation evidence.

candidates.reason: Below threshold and duplicate of recent post 98b4f6281cc3de4ecdfa95f6: both target online shops and customer inbox/email communication; the workflow/customer overlap applies despite the restock-specific trigger.

rejected.title: Self-hostable P2P voice app enthusiasm
rejected.reason: The only excerpt says “I loved how simple and self-hostable they were.” It describes a preference, not a concrete chore, repeated problem or request for a service, so no demand-backed experiment can be scored without inventing a task.

rejected.title: Features alongside a size chart app
rejected.reason: The excerpt says the poster is looking for features to build alongside a size chart app, but identifies no requested feature or concrete customer chore. A bounded experiment would require inventing the task.

rejected.title: Shopify App Store review delay
rejected.reason: The excerpt describes uncertainty about a pending app review, but no specific task beyond asking how to proceed. This is a one-off support problem, not a concrete recurring chore for a scoped service.

steps.message: Assessed all seven assigned discussion identities. Four concrete tasks were scored; each is below threshold or excluded for the stated one-off/duplicate reason. Three excerpts do not support a concrete chore. No post proposed.
